headline: Grammar Boss: Write and Say It Right
problemStatement: Grammar practice is easier to remember when students apply a rule to a sentence and then hear how the corrected version sounds. Grammar Boss generates a targeted challenge, collects student sentences, and turns the review into an anonymous class correction and read-aloud.
outcomes: Apply a selected grammar target in an original sentence.
Notice word-level corrections and explain how they improve meaning or form.
Practice speaking by reading and repeating a corrected sentence aloud.
howItWorks: Choose a grammar target and topic. The game presents a short task and a rule card with an example to guide student writing.
Students submit sentences on phones or take turns responding. During a race, a model sentence can be held to peek at without exposing it to the class immediately.
The review celebrates a top sentence by name when appropriate, then fixes other sentences together anonymously with removed words struck through and corrections highlighted.
A Say it right step invites the top student to read a corrected sentence aloud and the class to repeat it.
teacherUseCases: Use a recent grammar lesson as the target, then ask students to create an example connected to the current topic.
Keep the model sentence hidden during the challenge and reveal it after learners have had time to form their own answer.

faq.q: Can the class see a model answer while students work?
faq.a: The model sentence is hidden behind a hold-to-peek control during the race and shown after the challenge. The rule and example card remain available as support.

faq.q: How does the review protect student privacy?
faq.a: The top sentence may be celebrated by name, while the remaining sentences are corrected anonymously as a class rather than displayed in a named score-by-score parade.

faq.q: What does Say it right do?
faq.a: The top student reads the corrected sentence aloud, then the class repeats it. This adds a spoken fluency step after written grammar practice.

faq.q: Does Grammar Boss focus on one rule at a time?
faq.a: The challenge is generated for a selected grammar target, and the rule card shows a relevant explanation and example. Students apply that target in their own sentence.
